sentences.text: Banji was a small, lightly built, bipedal ground-dwelling carnivore that lived about 66 million years ago in what is now China.
It possessed a tall, crested skull similar to other oviraptorids, featuring an unusually long nasal opening that extended nearly to the eye socket along the crest.
The sides of this crest were uniquely adorned with vertical striations, and it had grooves on the top of its lower jaw.
The genus contains only one known species, Banji long, which means striped crest dragon in Chinese.
The fossil was donated to the Chinese Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology by an amateur collector who found it near Ganzhou in Jiangxi Province.
Banji was first described by Xu Xing and Feng-Lu Han in 2010.
Banji is classified in the order Saurischia, suborder Theropoda, and family Oviraptoridae.
Banji lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
In 2024, Andrea Cau suggested that Banji might represent an immature individual of the contemporary Corythoraptor, potentially making it a senior synonym.
